source: ACIAR Monograph No. 146a, "ដំណាំសំណែកសៀង" [Soybean Growers Manual], Belfield S., Brown C., Martin M. (eds.), New South Wales Department of Primary Industries / Murdoch University / CARDI / ACIAR, 2012
text: Weed management: the manual stresses that soybean is a weak early competitor against weeds, so weed control in the first 4–6 weeks after planting has an outsized effect on final yield. Options covered include pre-emergence and post-emergence herbicides — glyphosate and paraquat are both discussed for pre-planting burn-down of existing vegetation, with the manual explaining the different modes of action (glyphosate systemic/translocated, paraquat fast-acting contact) and cautioning that paraquat is highly toxic to humans and needs careful handling; selective post-emergence herbicides for grass weeds (fluazifop, quizalofop) and broadleaf weeds (fomesafen) are also named with rates. Manual/mechanical weeding (hand-hoeing, inter-row cultivation) is presented as the fallback for farmers without herbicide access, timed to before weeds compete seriously with the crop and before weeds themselves set seed.
